title: The criterion
hookLine: the book that separates right from wrong (25:1)

lines: IT SHOWS WHICH WAY IS NORTH.
cards: A ship's compass doesn't tell you where you want to go. It doesn't make the decision. It does one thing: it shows which way north is, so every other choice can be measured against it.
Without it, at night, in fog, all directions feel the same. Surah Al-Furqan opens by giving the Qur'an a name that works a little like that. Not the book, not the reading.
A name that means: the thing that tells two things apart.

teach.b: Pickthall: "Blessed is He Who hath revealed unto His slave the Criterion (of right and wrong), that he may be a warner to the peoples." The Criterion is al-furqan.
Its root, f-r-q, means to separate, to part, to make a distinction. Faraqa: he divided. Firqa: a group that has split off.
Furqan is the thing that divides: true from false, right from wrong, the path from the drift. Pickthall's brackets say what the criterion tells apart. And the word isn't used only for this book.

teach.h: MUSA, AND THE DAY OF BADR.
teach.b: The Qur'an says Musa and Harun were given al-furqan too. It calls the day of the battle of Badr yawm al-furqan, the day of distinction, when two sides met and the difference between them became plain.
And in Surah Al-Anfal there's a promise: if you are mindful of God, He will give you a furqan.
That one is inside a person: a sense of the difference, sharpened by taqwa, that helps you see which way to go when the options blur.
Tradition gives 'Umar ibn al-Khattab the title al-Faruq, the one who distinguishes, for how clearly he drew that line.
So furqan works on three levels: a book, a day, and a faculty inside you.
This week was full of differences: light and dark, the rumor and the good assumption, the first look and the second, walking in and knocking, the oath and the pardon.
Furqan is the name for the thing that tells them apart.

how: Muslims use al-Furqan as one of the names of the Qur'an, alongside al-Kitab and adh-Dhikr, and teachers cite 8:29 when speaking of the clarity that comes with mindfulness of God.

o: a chapter that splits the Qur'an into halves
a group that has split away from the rest
the criterion: what tells right from wrong

games.q: the word furqan — tap the pairs.

s: al-Furqan is used in the Qur'an only for the Qur'an itself
it is also used for what Musa and Harun were given, and for the day of Badr.
Pickthall adds 'of right and wrong' in brackets
to show what the criterion distinguishes.
the Qur'an promises a furqan to those who are mindful of God
Surah Al-Anfal says so: an inner sense of the difference.

games.q: two choices look the same in the fog. you have the Qur'an's furqan to help. what does it do?
o: it makes the decision for you.
it shows the difference, so you can choose.
it tells you to wait until the fog clears.
games.why: a furqan separates: like a compass, it doesn't steer the ship, it shows which way is which.

practice: Bring to mind one choice you've been leaving fuzzy: a reply you keep putting off, a habit you half-want to drop, a yes you mean as a no.
Hold the two options side by side, and ask which one you'd be glad, a year from now, to have chosen. If you pray, you can ask for a furqan.

wordCard.voice: Furqan. The criterion, the thing that tells right from wrong: a name for the Qur'an, for the day of Badr, and for a clarity inside a mindful person. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: furqan, criterion; from the root f-r-q, to separate.

carryVoice: Your line: tell right from wrong. A book, a day, and a clarity inside you. That's the week.

sources.q: Blessed is He Who hath revealed unto His slave the Criterion (of right and wrong), that he may be a warner to the peoples.
